report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Requirements are vague and stakeholder-driven; no defined success criteria or technology stack; high uncertainty in scope and deliverable form (build vs. buy decision unresolved).

project_understanding.primary_goal: Replace spreadsheet-based tracking with a centralized system to provide leadership visibility across teams.
project_understanding.beneficiary: Multiple teams and leadership (specific teams not named).
project_understanding.trigger: Current spreadsheet-based tracking is perceived as messy; leadership has requested visibility.
success_definition: Leadership has visibility into tracked items
Teams stop using spreadsheets for this purpose
supporting_quotes: We want something better for tracking stuff across teams.
People are using spreadsheets and it's messy.

assumption_log.what: Build vs. buy decision will be made before detailed planning begins; assuming internal build is the path forward for this plan.
assumption_log.why: Input mentions 'maybe an app' and 'could buy something' without resolution. A plan cannot proceed without knowing whether we are building, buying, or hybrid. Assuming build allows decomposition; buy decision would change project type entirely.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline requires accepted requirements and decision authority.
assumption_log.consequence: If buy decision is made, entire project plan (phases, tasks, staffing) becomes invalid. Procurement timeline, vendor evaluation, and contract negotiation replace development phases.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows planning to proceed without stakeholder delay. Risks: if buy is chosen, plan must be scrapped and replaced with procurement process.

assumption_log.what: Specific teams and data being tracked are unknown; assuming a single shared tracking system for multiple teams (not team-specific tools).
assumption_log.why: Input says 'across teams' but does not name which teams or what they track. Assuming a shared system is the most common interpretation of 'across teams' for internal tools.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 13.2 — Stakeholder requirements must be documented before execution.
assumption_log.consequence: If each team needs a separate system or if tracking domain is highly specialized (e.g., financial compliance vs. project tasks), architecture and scope change significantly.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows phase structure to be drafted. Risks: if actual scope is team-specific or domain-specific, feature set and complexity are underestimated.

assumption_log.what: Timeline 'soon' is interpreted as 8–12 weeks; no hard deadline provided.
assumption_log.why: Input states 'soon' without a specific date. For internal tools, 'soon' typically means 2–3 months. Assuming 10 weeks as midpoint allows schedule baseline to be created.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 6.4 — Schedule baseline derived from scope definition and resource constraints.
assumption_log.consequence: If 'soon' means 4 weeks, plan is not viable and requires aggressive scoping. If 'soon' means 6 months, plan is overly conservative.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows timeline estimation without stakeholder clarification. Risks: if actual deadline is significantly different, schedule baseline becomes invalid.

assumption_log.what: Budget is assumed to be $50,000–$100,000 (mid-range for internal tool build with 3–4 person team over 10 weeks).
assumption_log.why: Input says 'flexible but not huge.' For internal software, 'not huge' typically means under $150k. Assuming mid-range allows cost estimation without stakeholder input.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 7.2 — Cost estimation requires defined scope and resource plan.
assumption_log.consequence: If actual budget is $20k, scope must be cut to MVP only. If actual budget is $200k, plan is under-resourced.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows staffing plan to be drafted. Risks: if budget is significantly lower, team size and timeline become infeasible.

assumption_log.what: Team composition is assumed to be 1 PM, 2 developers (1 frontend, 1 backend), 1 QA engineer, 0.5 UX designer — total ~3.5 FTE.
assumption_log.why: Input states 'Team TBD' with no specification. For a TYPE_A project of 10 weeks, a 3–4 person team is standard. Assuming this composition allows task decomposition and staffing plan.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — Resource estimation tied to WBS and project duration.
assumption_log.consequence: If actual team is 1 person, timeline doubles or scope must be cut to 50%. If actual team is 6+ people, plan is over-resourced and budget is wasted.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows phase percentages and task hours to be assigned. Risks: if team size is significantly different, entire schedule and budget baseline becomes invalid.

assumption_log.what: Technology stack is assumed to be modern web stack (React/Vue frontend, Node.js or Python backend, PostgreSQL database, cloud hosting) — no legacy constraints assumed.
assumption_log.why: Input does not specify technology. Assuming modern stack is standard for new internal tools and allows architecture to be drafted without stakeholder input.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 4.2 — Project charter should define technology constraints; absence implies flexibility.
assumption_log.consequence: If legacy stack is mandated (e.g., .NET, Oracle), development timeline increases 20–30%. If specific vendor lock-in is required, architecture changes.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows task decomposition without architecture review. Risks: if stack is constrained, tasks and effort estimates become invalid.

assumption_log.what: Success criteria are assumed to be: (1) system is adopted by all target teams within 30 days of launch, (2) spreadsheet usage drops to zero, (3) leadership can generate visibility reports in < 5 minutes.
assumption_log.why: Input mentions 'leadership wants visibility' and 'messy spreadsheets' but does not define measurable success. Assuming adoption and visibility metrics are standard for this type of tool.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 — Project success requires defined, measurable acceptance criteria.
assumption_log.consequence: If success is defined differently (e.g., 'all teams use it' vs. 'leadership has visibility'), UAT and go-live criteria change. If no adoption target is set, project may be deemed failed even if technically complete.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows UAT and Phase 4 acceptance criteria to be drafted. Risks: if actual success definition is different, project may fail acceptance despite meeting assumed criteria.

assumption_log.what: Stakeholder approval of scope, timeline, and budget is assumed to be pending; no written sign-off mentioned in input.
assumption_log.why: Input is a request, not a charter. No mention of stakeholder approval, steering committee, or formal project kickoff.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 13.2 — Stakeholder requirements must be documented and approved before execution.
assumption_log.consequence: If stakeholders do not approve the assumed scope, timeline, or budget, project cannot proceed to execution. Plan becomes invalid.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows planning to proceed without approval delay. Risks: if stakeholders reject assumptions, entire plan must be reworked.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Frontend and Backend developers must be full-time and cannot be shared with other projects; PM must be available for all phases; QA must be full-time during Phases 3–4.

phases.name: Discovery & Design
milestones: Tracking requirements documented and signed off

tasks.name: Conduct stakeholder interviews to define what 'tracking stuff' means
tasks.definition_of_done: Interview notes document specific tracking use cases, data fields, and team workflows; stakeholder sign-off on scope summary.

tasks.name: Create user personas for target teams
tasks.definition_of_done: Personas document user roles, workflows, and pain points; reviewed and approved by PM.

tasks.name: Define success metrics and acceptance criteria
tasks.definition_of_done: Success metrics document adoption target, visibility requirements, and measurable acceptance criteria; stakeholder sign-off.

tasks.name: Design system architecture and data model
tasks.definition_of_done: Architecture diagram, data schema, and API contract documented; tech lead review completed.

tasks.name: Create wireframes for core tracking UI
tasks.definition_of_done: Wireframes cover main tracking views, data entry, and reporting; stakeholder feedback incorporated.

tasks.name: Obtain stakeholder sign-off on scope, timeline, and budget
tasks.definition_of_done: Written approval from leadership and team representatives on scope, 10-week timeline, and budget estimate.

phases.name: Core Development
milestones: Backend API endpoints for core tracking implemented
Frontend UI for data entry and basic views working

tasks.name: Set up development environment and CI/CD pipeline
tasks.definition_of_done: Developers can deploy code to staging environment; automated tests run on every commit.

tasks.name: Implement database schema and migrations
tasks.definition_of_done: Schema deployed to staging; all tables created with proper indexes and constraints.

tasks.name: Build authentication and authorization layer
tasks.definition_of_done: Users can log in via SSO; role-based access control enforced; audit log created for all access.

tasks.name: Implement core tracking API endpoints (create, read, update, delete)
tasks.definition_of_done: All CRUD endpoints tested and documented; API contract matches Phase 1 design.

tasks.name: Build frontend data entry form and validation
tasks.definition_of_done: Form accepts all required fields; client-side validation works; form submits to API.

tasks.name: Build frontend list view and basic filtering
tasks.definition_of_done: Users can view all tracking items; filter by team and status; pagination works.

tasks.name: Conduct internal demo with stakeholders
tasks.definition_of_done: Demo completed; stakeholder feedback documented; direction confirmed before proceeding to Phase 3.

phases.name: Integration & Edge Cases
milestones: Reporting views for leadership visibility completed

tasks.name: Implement advanced filtering and search
tasks.definition_of_done: Users can filter by multiple fields and search by keyword; performance acceptable on 10k+ records.

tasks.name: Build leadership visibility dashboard and reporting views
tasks.definition_of_done: Dashboard shows summary metrics, team breakdowns, and status distribution; leadership can generate reports in < 5 minutes.

tasks.name: Implement data export (CSV, Excel)
tasks.definition_of_done: Users can export filtered data to CSV and Excel; formatting is clean and usable.

tasks.name: Conduct security review and implement fixes
tasks.definition_of_done: Security review completed; OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities checked; fixes implemented and verified.

tasks.name: Handle edge cases and error scenarios
tasks.definition_of_done: System handles null values, duplicate entries, concurrent updates, and API timeouts gracefully; error messages are user-friendly.

tasks.name: Execute functional test suite for all features
tasks.definition_of_done: Test cases cover all user workflows; pass rate ≥ 95%; critical bugs logged and prioritized.

tasks.name: Conduct user acceptance testing with target teams
tasks.definition_of_done: UAT completed with representatives from each target team; sign-off obtained; feedback incorporated.

tasks.name: Perform performance testing and optimization
tasks.definition_of_done: System handles 100 concurrent users; response time < 2 seconds for all views; database queries optimized.

tasks.name: Resolve critical and high-priority bugs
tasks.definition_of_done: All critical bugs fixed and verified; high-priority bugs resolved or deferred to Phase 2 with stakeholder approval.

tasks.name: Conduct accessibility audit (WCAG 2.1 AA)
tasks.definition_of_done: Accessibility audit completed; WCAG 2.1 AA compliance verified; fixes implemented for any failures.

tasks.name: Deploy to production and verify smoke tests
tasks.definition_of_done: Application deployed to production; smoke tests pass; monitoring and alerting active.

tasks.name: Write operational runbooks and troubleshooting guides
tasks.definition_of_done: Runbooks document deployment, backup, recovery, and common troubleshooting scenarios; reviewed by ops team.

tasks.name: Conduct go-live training and handoff to support team
tasks.definition_of_done: Support team trained on system operation; escalation procedures documented; post-launch support plan established.

risk_register.description: If stakeholder requirements remain vague (what 'tracking stuff' means is not defined), then scope will expand during development and timeline will slip.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder interviews in Phase 1 reveal conflicting or incomplete requirements; scope creep requests appear during Phase 2.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct detailed stakeholder interviews in Phase 1 (T1); document specific use cases and data fields; obtain written sign-off on scope before Phase 2 begins (T6).
risk_register.contingency: If scope expands mid-project, invoke change control process; defer non-critical features to Phase 2 release; extend timeline or reduce scope to maintain deadline.

risk_register.description: If timeline 'soon' is interpreted as 4 weeks instead of 10 weeks, project is not viable and requires aggressive scope reduction or team expansion.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder clarifies deadline is 4 weeks; critical path analysis shows 10 weeks minimum for current scope.
risk_register.mitigation: Clarify exact deadline in Phase 1 kickoff meeting (T6); document deadline in writing; establish change control process for timeline changes.
risk_register.contingency: If deadline is 4 weeks, reduce scope to MVP (authentication, basic data entry, list view only); defer reporting and advanced features to Phase 2.

risk_register.description: If team composition is not confirmed (Team TBD), project cannot start and timeline will slip due to ramp-up delays.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 start date arrives; developers not assigned or not available; shared resources pulled to other projects.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm team composition and full-time availability in writing before Phase 1 ends (T6); establish resource commitment from HR/management; identify backup resources for critical roles.
risk_register.contingency: If team is unavailable, delay Phase 2 start or reduce scope to match available capacity; hire contractors or defer non-critical features.

risk_register.description: If success criteria are not defined (what 'leadership visibility' means is ambiguous), project may be deemed failed even if technically complete.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 4 UAT reveals stakeholders expected different reporting views or metrics; acceptance criteria not met.
risk_register.mitigation: Define measurable success criteria in Phase 1 (T3); document adoption targets, visibility requirements, and acceptance metrics; obtain stakeholder sign-off.
risk_register.contingency: If success criteria are unclear at UAT, conduct stakeholder workshop to align on definition; adjust acceptance criteria or extend Phase 4 for additional development.

risk_register.description: If technology stack is not specified and team has no experience with chosen stack, development velocity will be 30–50% lower than estimated.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 begins; developers unfamiliar with chosen framework or database; ramp-up takes 2+ weeks.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm technology stack in Phase 1 (T4); verify team experience with chosen stack; allocate 1 week ramp-up time in Phase 2 schedule.
risk_register.contingency: If team lacks experience, hire contractor or pair with experienced engineer; extend Phase 2 timeline by 1–2 weeks; reduce scope if timeline cannot be extended.

risk_register.description: If build vs. buy decision is not made, project planning is based on false assumption and may be invalidated by procurement process.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 completes; stakeholder decides to buy off-the-shelf solution instead of building; project plan becomes invalid.
risk_register.mitigation: Resolve build vs. buy decision before Phase 1 ends (T6); document decision rationale; if buy is chosen, transition to procurement process.
risk_register.contingency: If buy decision is made, cancel build project; initiate vendor evaluation and procurement process; timeline and budget change significantly.

risk_register.description: If QA engineer is not allocated, testing will be inadequate and critical bugs will reach production.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 3 begins; no QA resource available; developers test their own code; test coverage < 50%.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm QA engineer allocation in staffing plan; allocate minimum 25% of development hours to QA (PMBOK 8.2); include QA in Phase 2 start.
risk_register.contingency: If QA is unavailable, hire contractor QA engineer; extend Phase 4 timeline for manual testing; reduce scope to reduce testing burden.

risk_register.description: If external system integrations are required (e.g., LDAP, email, third-party APIs) and not scoped, Phase 3 will be delayed.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 completes; stakeholder requests integration with external system not in original scope; API documentation unavailable.
risk_register.mitigation: Identify all external system dependencies in Phase 1 (T1); confirm API access and documentation; include integration tasks in Phase 3 plan.
risk_register.contingency: If integration is required but not scoped, defer to Phase 2 release; implement workaround (manual data sync) for MVP; extend Phase 3 timeline.

risk_register.description: If security and compliance requirements are not defined, security review in Phase 3 may reveal significant rework needed.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 3 security review (T17) reveals authentication, encryption, or audit logging requirements not implemented.
risk_register.mitigation: Define security requirements in Phase 1 (T1); confirm compliance obligations (SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR); include security engineer in Phase 2 design.
risk_register.contingency: If security issues are found late, allocate additional Phase 3 time for fixes; defer non-critical security features to Phase 2; conduct re-review before Phase 4.

risk_register.description: If stakeholder approval is not obtained in Phase 1, project cannot proceed to Phase 2 and timeline will slip.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 completes; stakeholder does not approve scope, timeline, or budget; project is blocked pending re-planning.
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain written stakeholder sign-off on scope, timeline, and budget before Phase 1 ends (T6); establish steering committee for approval authority.
risk_register.contingency: If approval is delayed, conduct stakeholder workshop to address concerns; adjust scope, timeline, or budget as needed; re-submit for approval.

staffing_plan.notes: Full-time PM required for all phases; owns stakeholder alignment, scope definition, and UAT. Critical path tasks: T1, T3, T6, T13, T20, T26.
Full-time backend developer required for Phases 2–4; owns API implementation, database design, and backend optimization. Critical path tasks: T10, T14, T18, T22.
Full-time frontend developer required for Phases 2–4; owns UI implementation, data entry forms, and reporting views. Supports critical path indirectly through T10 dependency.
Full-time QA engineer required for Phases 3–4; owns functional testing, UAT coordination, and accessibility audit. Minimum 25% of dev hours (180h × 25% = 45h); allocated 80h exceeds minimum.
Part-time UX designer (50% allocation) for Phases 1–2; owns persona definition, wireframing, and UI design. Front-loaded; not on critical path but supports T5 and T11.
Part-time solution architect (50% allocation) for Phase 1 only; owns architecture design and technology stack selection. Supports T4; not on critical path.
Part-time DevOps engineer (30% Phase 2, 70% Phase 5); owns CI/CD setup, deployment, and operational handoff. Back-loaded; supports T7, T24, T25.
Part-time security engineer (50% allocation) for Phase 3 only; owns security review and compliance audit. Supports T17; not on critical path but HIGH impact if missing.
